boot.evidence: A guest booted for this run: every measurement below is a command executed inside it through the console channel.

exec_length_limit_enforced.evidence: Commands above 2000 bytes are refused with exit 64 and {"error":"command too long","limit":2000}; commands at or below it are delivered. Over-limit probes in this run: [(2002, 64), (2500, 64)].

delivery_is_bounded_in_time.evidence: Under the limit, delivery is not truncated but it is slow, and the cost grows with length: 500 B -> 498 bytes echoed, done=True, 1 s; 1200 B -> 1198 bytes echoed, done=True, 0 s; 2000 B -> 1998 bytes echoed, done=True, 0 s; 2002 B -> 0 bytes echoed, done=False, 0 s; 2500 B -> 0 bytes echoed, done=False, 0 s. The slowest delivered command was 500 bytes in 1 s.

known_limits_observed: the console channel is one line per command, so a larger command costs seconds, not milliseconds; long scripts belong in bench/guest-put.sh chunks
notes: Issue #1 in docs/ISSUES.md. Three silent truncations were found and fixed (argv join overflow, a 1024-byte request buffer, a single read() into 512 bytes); what remains is the measured cost of delivery, which is why the limit is a refusal at 2000 bytes instead of a bigger buffer. docs/RUNTIME-CONTRACT.md 9a carries the same table.
